subject: POC sprint charter & model pairing — DataVesta onramp
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Grant <alyssa@datavesta.com>, Michael Stone <michael.stone@datavesta.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap and proposed POC sprint charter (DataVesta)

Hi Alyssa & Michael,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and clear priorities. Quick recap and a proposed two-week POC sprint to validate latency, cost, and accuracy for your search augmentation use case.

Key business goals you called out:
- Improve query-answer latency for end-users (target: 95th percentile latency under 400ms)
- Keep per-1k-query inference cost below our current benchmark (rough target: under $6/1k; we will refine after baseline)
- Support Spanish (es-ES) and Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) for 20% of traffic initially
- Maintain precision on domain-specific retrievals (top-1 factual correctness > 88% on your internal sample set)

Proposed POC sprint (2 weeks) — high level:
1) Week 0 (prep): exchange redacted sample prompts, 1k representative queries (we have a template attached datavesta-eval-prompts.csv), and access details for a staging S3 bucket
2) Week 1: baseline run on Meta LLaMA 2 13B (int8) hosted via Redwood API; collect latency, cost, and quality metrics on your prompt set
3) Week 2: evaluate fallback variants (Mistral 7B int8 and a trimmed 3B local quantized variant for throughput), run A/B for multilingual slices, finalize acceptance checks and handoff plan

Model pairing suggestion (initial):
- Primary: Meta LLaMA 2 13B (int8 quantized) — balances quality and cost for retrieval-augmented workflows
- Fallback 1: Mistral 7B (int8) — lower cost, good latency for bulk traffic or burst/backfill
- Fallback 2: Local 3B int4 variant — for extremely low-latency or air-gapped requests if needed

Success criteria (examples we propose for acceptance):
- Latency: 95th percentile under 400ms for English; under 500ms for es/pt slices
- Cost: average token/inference unit cost below $6/1k at projected QPS
- Quality: Top-1 answer accuracy >= 88% on your annotated sample; NPS/internal dev satisfaction 4/5 on handoff

Owners and roles:
- DataVesta: Alyssa (PM) — provide sample data and sign off on eval prompts; Michael — technical contact for S3 access
- Redwood: Soojin (AE) — project lead and commercial owner; Connor (SE) — technical lead for benchmarks and model pairing; Dylan (Sales Eng) — commercial/pricing alignment

Attachments: datavesta-eval-prompts.csv (sample prompts template), datavesta-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP), model-latency-estimates.pdf (reference)

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm you can share a redacted sample set (1k queries) by Tue, May 19
- I will schedule a technical kickoff with Connor for Wed, May 25 to run initial benchmarks
- Dylan will follow up with a preliminary cost estimate once we confirm expected QPS

If that looks good I will ship an updated MAP and a short sprint charter this afternoon.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed POC sprint charter (DataVesta)

Thanks, Soojin — this is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying items: 

1) Timeline: May 25 kickoff is fine for us. We need internal signoff from Legal on a short data processing addendum; expect that by Tue, May 19 but I will confirm.
2) Evaluation prompts: I will prioritize a multilingual slice (200 es/pt queries) from our corpus and share the redacted S3 keys by Mon EOD.
3) Pricing: can you include a back-of-envelope cost for the two-week run (estimate for Meta LLaMA 2 13B int8 primary plus 7B fallback)? That will help our procurement team move quickly.

Also, can you attach the MAP you mentioned in an XLS or Google Sheet (we prefer Google Sheets)?

Appreciate the clarity — looking forward to the kickoff.

— Alyssa

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed POC sprint charter (DataVesta)

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation, Alyssa.

Quick updates: 
- I converted the MAP to a Google Sheet and shared the link (see related_links). You should have view/comment access; if you need edit I can open it.
- Back-of-envelope cost: for a two-week active run at your anticipated QPS (~2 rps average with bursts to 10 rps):
  • LLaMA 2 13B int8 primary: estimated compute + token cost ~ $2,800 - $3,600 total for the two weeks (depends on exact sequence length distribution)
  • Mistral 7B fallback: incremental cost if used for 30% of requests ~ $650 - $900
  • Ad hoc local 3B runs: negligible infra cost but ops time to set up (~4-8 engineer hours)
These are roughs; Dylan will produce a formal quote after we agree on the acceptance criteria and expected traffic profile.

Prep ask for DataVesta before kickoff:
- Redacted sample (1k queries) including a 200-sample multilingual slice (es/pt) by Tue May 19
- Temporary S3 read credentials or a shared Drive link with the sample data
- Any non-functional constraints (e.g., must remain in us-west or VPN-only)

Connor, can you confirm you have bandwidth to run the baseline benchmarks the week of May 25 and whether you prefer the sample set in CSV or newline-delimited JSON?

If Alyssa confirms the sample delivery timeline, I will lock the kickoff and share a calendar invite for May 25 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Soojin

Soojin / Dylan — quick internal note (looping here to confirm readiness ahead of the kickoff).

I can take the SE lead for the May 25 run. My plan:
- Prefer sample in newline-delimited JSON (one object per line with keys: id, lang, query, context) 
- I will run the baseline on LLaMA 2 13B int8 and Mistral 7B int8 and capture: p50/p90/p95 latency, token counts, and a small accuracy script comparing top-1 to your annotated answers.
- I attached a short CSV with my template for latency capture and the preliminary scripts (model-latency-estimates.pdf is a short reference of the expected ranges).

If Alyssa can share credentials by EOD Mon, May 24 I will have the first pass metrics ready within 24 hours of kickoff.
